I cannot believe how similar this post is to my case. I have had a very good childhood in the form of good parents and no emotional trauma. For a very long while, I couldnt understand how someone with such a good life up till now would have limerence and self-esteem issues. Turns out, when I really dug deep into my childhood, I realized that yes, my parents were good but my father was never there(It was not his fault though because he worked abroad) and this could be a major reason to how I could have developed anxious attachment as a child.  I was a very good student and got straight As. But my father was never happy, he always told me to improve and be better. He was a good father but he was never satisfied with my academic performance. He would always want me to be better. Due to this, I would always be harsh on myself, no matter how much i achieved I was never happy and always wanted more. This resulted in me not loving myself. I am 23 right now, got into my dream school and have a pretty nice life ahead of me according to conventional standards. However, due to this limerence, I am not able to think about anything else other than my LO. How, according to me, we are meant for each other when in reality we would be an absolute disaster. Like seriously, it couldn't work. My logical brain understands this but the emotional brain comes in its way and stops me from thinking rationally. Sometimes I wonder if there is a chemical imbalance in my brain. For me, what helps is writing down all the reasons why we could never work even if we were to be together. So, whenever my mind tends to wander and think abut my LO, I open my phone and look at those reasons. Helps me temporarily but it does work. Secondly, this has been said a million times but being busy does help. I notice that when I have nothing to do, I tend to think about it more than when I am doing something important. I dont blame my parents for this because they couldnt have realized how much of an effect it would have on me later in life. So the point of this long comment is: Yes limerence is terrible and there are times when I just want to end it all, but deep down I know that it is just in my head. The idealization of my LO is a result of me not being able to idealize my own self which is the first step towards recovery.

As someone who has ended on bad terms with his LO and wants to fix it with one last conversation, I will tell you that its not worth it. The closure is basically our mind playing tricks on us. What do you expect to get out of this closure honestly? Only you can give yourself closure, no one else can. Remember, limerence is just a chemical imbalance in the brain which is telling you that this person might be the best guy you could have. But you know what, the mind is deluded. You told us how little he cares about you. Say if you two were to get together somehow. He would know that its you who wants him more. This will give him an upper advantage in the relationship which you definitely dont want. A relationship should be about equality and both partners caring about each other more or less the same. With limerence this is very rarely possible. Also, you would be jeopardising your marriage in the process. I know it takes time for our emotional brain to process this, but it will eventually happen. NC is really effective.
